content: Take this medication orally with meals as directed by your doctor, typically one to two times daily. For certain conditions, such as hydatid disease, your doctor may recommend taking this medication in treatment cycles (e.g., twice daily with meals for 28 days, followed by a 2-week break). It is important to use this medication consistently to achieve the maximum benefit. To help you remember, take it at the same time(s) each day. Continue taking this medication for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. Other medications, such as corticosteroids or anti-seizure drugs, may also be prescribed to manage your condition. Avoid consuming grapefruit or grapefruit juice while using this medication unless your doctor or pharmacist confirms it is safe to do so. Grapefruit can increase the likelihood of side effects associated with this medication. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, headache, or temporary hair loss. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. If you are in the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before taking albendazole, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other benzimidazole anthelmintic drugs (e.g., mebendazole), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may also cause liver problems. Since alcohol consumption increases the risk of liver complications, limit alcoholic beverages while using this medication. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. You should not become pregnant while using albendazole, as it may harm an unborn baby. Your doctor will likely order a pregnancy test before starting this medication. Discuss reliable forms of birth control to use during treatment and for three days after the last dose. This medication can pass into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In case of an overdose, if someone has severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes. Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., liver function tests, complete blood counts) should be performed before starting this medication and periodically during treatment. Attend all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
